raw_segments.text: This is the reason he is poor. And for a similar reason we are all poor in respect to a thousand savage comforts, though surrounded by luxuries. As Chapman sings,—
The farmer is endeavoring to solve the problem of a livelihood by a formula more complicated
than the problem itself. To get his shoestrings, he speculates in herds of cattle. With consummate
skill he has set his trap with a hair spring to catch comfort and independence, and then,
as he turned away, got his own leg into it. This is the reason he is poor, and for a similar
reason we are all poor in respect to a thousand savage comforts, though surrounded by luxuries.
